subject: Discovery recap — quick fit check & next step
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Bennet <alex.bennet@datahelm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — quick fit check & next step

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Short recap and a single ask: does this feel like something DataHelm should evaluate further right now?

Recap (high level):
- Primary ask: reduce inference cost for batch model scoring and enable low-latency feature extraction for spike hours.
- Current infra: on-prem GPU pool + burst to cloud; pain: unpredictable token costs and cold-start latency.
- Success metric: 30–40% reduction in per-token inference cost, <150ms P50 for short sequences during peak.

What we demo'd / proposed:
- Redwood inference runtime for mixed on-prem/cloud routing; automatic KV caching for repeat prefixes; cost-aware routing to spot/ reserved capacity.
- Typical lift: customers in your vertical see 20–50% unit cost reduction after batching + prefix caching improvements.

Attachments & links: discovery-notes.pdf (notes + configurations we discussed), demo-recording.mp4 (screen capture). Also shared a 15-min booking link if you want a short follow-up: https://cal.com/monica/15min

Proposed next step (one ask):
- Can you confirm whether reducing inference unit cost is a current priority for DataHelm this quarter, and if so, would you like a short tech validation (15–30m) to go over quantization/training artifacts we saw in your config?

If helpful, Ben is copied and can join for technical details.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachment: discovery-notes.pdf (PDF, 72KB)
Attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (MP4, 18MB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Bennet <alex.bennet@datahelm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Checking in on fit — quick follow up

Alex —

Looping back on my note from last week. Quick check: is the cost/timing problem we discussed something you’re actively prioritizing this quarter? If not, totally fine — a 1‑sentence signal is super helpful for our planning.

If it is, I can:
- Book 15 minutes to run through a narrow validation plan (Ben can join)
- Share a short comparison (initial estimate) for your most common scoring job

No pressure — if you’re the wrong person for timing updates, can you point me to the right owner?

Best,
Monica

From: Alex Bennet <alex.bennet@datahelm.com>

Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datahelm.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checking in on fit — quick follow up

Monica —

Thanks for the follow-up and the clear notes. Short answers:
- Is reducing inference unit cost a priority? Yes, it’s in our Q4 roadmap and we need to show cost improvements for the retraining pipeline.
- Fit: What you showed looks promising — especially the KV caching for repeating prefixes (we have lots of repeated context in batch jobs).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Please send a 1‑page sketch of a narrow pilot (objectives, approx timeline, minimal data access required). That will help me get internal buy‑in quickly.
2) Can you include a rough ballpark TCO delta for our most common nightly scoring job (I’ll share the job size via separate email).

I’m copying Priya (in infra) who can own the technical validation. We should aim for a short call next week once we have the sketch.

Thanks —
Alex Bennet
Director of ML Engineering
DataHelm Inc.
alex.bennet@datahelm.com
